messages.subject: Re: Comparing eigen to nimEigen
parts:
Hi Tom, in general, in nimbleFunction code, we use the Eigen C++ package for linear algebra, so nimEigen uses Eigen. In contrast R's eigen uses LAPACK. So there may be numerical differences between Eigen and LAPACK for a given matrix.

For k.bad, it seems that LAPACK and Eigen give the same result.

For the transpose of k.bad, it appears there are numerical differences between LAPACK and Eigen. The result from Eigen has non-zero imaginary parts for the 4th and 5th eigenvalues, but those imaginary parts are very small (around 5 x 10^-18). NIMBLE doesn't handle complex numbers so in post-processing of the Eigen output, we turn the complex values into NaN values.

I'll file an issue for our development team so that we consider returning the real part in such cases where the imaginary part is negligible.

-chris
